title: Which Source Wins? Task-Dependent Reliance in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.17205v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) combine images and text, but when the two conflict and one becomes harder to read, it is unclear how a model shifts its reliance between them. We study this modality reallocation with a controlled setup: we degrade either the image or the text across four levels of legibility while keeping the other clean, and track how the model's preference changes. We build conflicts from GSM8K and SVAMP by pairing the rendered image of one arithmetic problem with the text of another, so the two sources support different answers. We also introduce ChartQA-Conflict, a manually reviewed benchmark of 229 chart-report conflicts with matched chart and table-image representations. We evaluate six open-weight VLMs using both generated answers and a length-normalized conditional log-likelihood margin. On GSM8K and SVAMP, five of six models shift more strongly away from degraded text than from degraded images. On ChartQA-Conflict,

tldr: 视觉语言模型在图像和文本冲突时，会根据任务类型调整依赖：在算术任务中，模型更倾向于依赖图像而非退化文本；在图表任务中，这种依赖模式可能不同。
en_tdlr: Vision-language models adjust reliance between image and text based on task type: in arithmetic tasks, models shift more strongly away from degraded text than degraded images, while in chart tasks, the pattern may differ.
